issues.title: Inconsistent FVEM trial and test space definitions

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \{v\in C(\bar{\Omega}):\ v|_K\ \text{is piecewise linear for all} \, K\in T_h\}
\{v\in L^2(\Omega):\ v|_{V_i}\ \text{is piecewise constant for all} \ V_i\in T_h^*\}
$\mathcal{N}_h$ denotes the set of all nodes with $N = |\mathcal{N}_h|$, and then define $\mathcal{N}_h^{0} = \mathcal{N}_h\cap\Omega$.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims that the previously defined full continuous piecewise-linear space and full dual-cell piecewise-constant space equal spans indexed only by interior nodes. The set-builder definitions actually admit boundary nodal basis functions and boundary-control-volume characteristic functions, whereas the asserted spans omit them. Thus the two descriptions impose different boundary degrees of freedom and do not define the same trial/test pair.
issues.overall_effect: The admissible discrete spaces and the action of the interior-node interpolation operators are ambiguous, although the surrounding homogeneous-boundary scheme makes the intended restricted spaces apparent.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define the spaces consistently with the interior degrees of freedom: take S_h to be the conforming piecewise-linear subspace of H_0^1(Ω), take S_h^* to be the span of the characteristic functions of control volumes associated with interior nodes, and use these restricted spaces consistently in the interpolation operators and homogeneous-boundary scheme.
issues.why_classification: This is a genuine definitional mismatch, not a uniquely forced transcription error, because using full spaces with separately imposed boundary constraints is also a coherent convention. The surrounding homogeneous-boundary formulation nevertheless makes a short, routine local repair clear, with no change to the method or its guarantees.

issues.title: Invalid H2 scope for the Delta-v L4 estimate

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
there exists a constant $C$ such that for all $\bmf{v}\in \bmf{H}^2$,
the following inequalities hold:

issues.failure_explanation: In two dimensions the old display quantifies over all v in H2. Such membership supplies second weak derivatives in L2 but does not supply grad Delta v in L2 or generally Delta v in L4. The final formula is therefore not a defined finite estimate on its advertised class.
issues.overall_effect: The last advertised Sobolev estimate has an overbroad domain. Later occurrences involving Delta v in L4 are made in higher-regularity settings, so their valid H3 instances do not depend on the false H2-wide scope.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Separate the final Δv L4 estimate from the H2-wide assertions and require Δv∈H1, for example by stating it for v∈H3. Keep the displayed inequality otherwise unchanged; later uses already occur under the needed higher regularity.
issues.why_classification: The estimate needs a genuine missing regularity premise, so it is not merely typographical. Adding that standard local qualification is routine and causes no downstream change, since no later result relies on an H2-only instance.

issues.title: Unsupported H3 stability under only Dirichlet data
issues.failure_explanation: For fixed Phi in X, the old lemma assumes only that the auxiliary solution vanishes on the boundary. That trace condition does not imply the higher-order trace conditions needed when testing through Delta squared and Delta cubed and integrating by parts. Consequently, the displayed H3 energy estimate is not derived; the preceding argument supports at most the weaker H2 conclusion adopted in version 2.
issues.overall_effect: The asserted H3 stability of the auxiliary solution is unsupported under the stated boundary hypotheses. H3 control would require additional compatibility conditions, while the lower-order H2 stability can be retained.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the lemma by the supported H2 stability statement ‖m̃(t)‖_{H2}≤C‖m̃_0‖_{H2} and remove the unsupported H3/H4 energy step, while retaining the same auxiliary equation and Dirichlet setting.
issues.why_classification: The repair is contained and leaves a recognizably comparable stability lemma, but losing one full derivative from the asserted conclusion is a meaningful limited weakening. It therefore exceeds a minor local correction without requiring global reconstruction or causing major mathematical loss.

issues.title: Incorrect mass-lumped energy identity in the auxiliary error proof
issues.failure_explanation: The pairing (xi,I_h*xi) is the mass-lumped quadratic form, not the ordinary L2 norm squared. Moreover, the old definition |||v|||_0=(v,I_h*v) scales quadratically, so its asserted linear equivalence with ||v||L2 cannot hold under arbitrary scalar rescaling. Consequently, the displayed L2 energy derivative in the proof of pro2 does not follow from the error equation.
issues.overall_effect: The Gronwall energy step establishing the auxiliary L2 estimate, and hence the use of that estimate in the nonlinear theorem, is not justified as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define the mass-lumped norm by |||v_h|||_0^2=(v_h,I_h^*v_h), state the corresponding square-root norm equivalence with the L2 norm, and replace each ordinary-L2 energy identification by the mass-lumped identity, in particular (∂_tξ,I_h^*ξ)=½∂_t|||ξ|||_0^2. Apply the equivalence after Gronwall to recover the same bounds in Proposition pro2 and its use in thm-error.
issues.why_classification: The proof uses an invalid energy identity, so mathematical correction is required rather than a mere renaming. The correction is standard, short mass-lumping bookkeeping and preserves both auxiliary convergence rates and the dependent theorem's invocation of them.

issues.title: Wrong coefficient in the auxiliary-error residual
issues.failure_explanation: Subtracting the auxiliary equations must retain their common reaction coefficient |grad Phi| squared. Replacing it by |Phi| squared means equ:error1 is not the error equation for the two problems stated in pro2, so the subsequent residual estimates do not prove the proposition as written.
issues.overall_effect: Both auxiliary error bounds lose their stated derivation, and thm-error cannot invoke pro2 until the source residual is corrected.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace |Φ|^2 by |∇Φ|^2 in the residual identity equ:error1 and in every estimate derived from that residual, and bound the corrected products using the existing regularity assumptions on Φ. The L2 and H1 rates in pro2, and hence its downstream use in thm-error, remain unchanged.
issues.why_classification: Although subtraction of the source equations uniquely identifies the correct coefficient, the proof subsequently estimates the wrong residual and thus requires mathematical checking beyond a pure transcription fix. The correction is local and routine and entails no new lemma, rate loss, or change of model.

issues.title: Missing nonlinear-to-discrete coefficient comparison

failure_location.quote: the FVEM scheme \eqref{auxiliary} is equivalent to the FVEM scheme \eqref{equ:LL-semi-discretized1}

issues.failure_explanation: The auxiliary estimate requires a prescribed coefficient Phi in X and compares continuous and discrete auxiliary problems using that same coefficient. The old proof instead sets Phi equal to a piecewise-linear discrete iterate, which is not generally in X, and declares the resulting linear auxiliary step equivalent to the nonlinear scheme. At finite iteration index the coefficient and unknown are different, and equality with the nonlinear solution requires a separately proved discrete fixed-point limit. Neither that limit nor the continuous-versus-discrete coefficient error is supplied in version 1.
issues.overall_effect: The optimal L2 and H1 spatial estimates for the nonlinear LL discretization do not follow from the auxiliary estimate as written, although the auxiliary estimate remains a distinct intermediate result.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Keep separate continuous Picard iterates, nonlinear discrete Picard iterates, and discrete auxiliary iterates using the continuous coefficient. Prove convergence of the discrete iteration on short time intervals, subtract the two discrete schemes to obtain the coefficient-difference residuals, and derive L2 and H1 stability recurrences that combine with pro2 to give O(h^2) and O(h) errors. Then pass to the fixed-point limit and concatenate the short intervals.
issues.why_classification: The false equivalence cannot be repaired by a notation change or a routine estimate; it requires a substantial new coefficient-comparison and discrete fixed-point argument. That argument is nevertheless contained within the paper's existing auxiliary/Picard framework and recovers the same model, norms, and optimal rates, so it avoids both global reconstruction and major mathematical loss.

issues.title: Unbound variable in the coercivity lemma
issues.failure_explanation: The universally quantified vector m_h never appears in the coercivity and boundedness formulas, while tilde m_h appears without a quantifier. Thus the literal lemma does not assert the estimates for the vector used in its formulas. The surrounding formulas and proof uniquely show that these names were intended to coincide.
issues.overall_effect: The supporting coercivity lemma is formally malformed, and its use in lem-Ah, pro2, and thm-error requires the intended variable binding.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change the quantifier to “for all m̃_h,v_h∈S_h,” or equivalently rename every occurrence of m̃_h in the formulas consistently to m_h. No formula or proof step otherwise changes, and the corrected binding applies unchanged through lem-Ah, pro2, and thm-error.
issues.why_classification: The surrounding statement, formulas, and proof uniquely force the two variable names to denote the same vector. A direct local renaming restores the binding without repairing any mathematical inference, so this is purely transcriptional.
